sentences.text: Andrewsornis stands as the tallest known member of the subfamily Patagornithinae, growing to 1.8 meters in height and weighing between 60 and 89 kilograms.
Its lower jaw measures 39 centimeters long and is notably slimmer than that of the related genus Phorusrhacos.
Fossil collector John Bernard Abbott first found remains on September 18, 1923, in Cabeza Blanca, Chubut Province, southern Argentina.
Paleontologist Bryan Patterson formally described the remains as the new species Andrewsornis abbotti in 1941.
In 2003, Herculano Alvarenga and Elizabeth Höfling established the subfamily Patagornithinae to group Andrewsornis with Andalgalornis.
A 2015 phylogenetic analysis by Degrange et al. placed Andrewsornis in a merged Phorusrhacinae clade in polytomy with Physornis and Phorusrhacos.
Fossils have been recovered from the Sarmiento Formation and possibly the Agua de la Piedra Formation.
The animal lived between 29 and 21 million years ago, spanning the Rupelian to Aquitanian stages.
